title: Introduce DNS-forwarder shadowing and deterministic SG naming for private control plane
author: Sana Iyer
description: Motivation: Private control plane rollouts sometimes experience DNS transient failure during cross-account peering and SG rotation. This PR introduces a lightweight, opt-in "shadowed" DNS forwarder that mirrors control plane DNS zones into a customer-managed private hosted zone and a deterministic security-group naming scheme to make policy and rotation idempotent across re-applies. What changed: Terraform module additions (control-plane/dns-forwarder, network/sg-naming); Helm chart values to enable the forwarder as a DaemonSet for on-prem installs; an upgrade job that creates provisional shadow zones and validates DNS propagation; a small operator-side hook for safe SG swaps during migration. Rollout plan: Default behavior is unchanged. Operators can enable the feature via the private-installer helm values or by setting enable_shadow_dns = true in the Terraform module. Rollout steps are documented in upgrade_notes.md and include preflight checks, staged canary in a single AZ, and automated rollback if propagation or endpoint auth fails. Backwards compatibility: The DNS forwarder is additive; when disabled the installer behaves identically to previous releases. The SG naming scheme will not change existing SGs unless the migration job is explicitly run; migration is reversible. Security considerations: forwarder binds to VPC endpoints only (ENIs are ephemeral) and uses cross-account endpoint authorization tokens; IAM policy changes are scoped and documented. Related work: ties into ENG-7221 (dns resiliency) and ENG-7304 (safer sg rotation).
